title: Can Small-Scale Data Poisoning Exacerbate Dialect-Linked Biases in Large Language Models?

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing toxicity scores (using Detoxify and Perspective API) and stereotype expression (using GPT-4o as an LLM-as-a-judge) in model outputs generated from semantically equivalent prompts written in African American Vernacular English (AAVE), Southern dialect, and Standard American English (SAE).

Using an LLM-as-a-judge to explicitly evaluate responses triggered by AAVE prompts for bias toward Black individuals (rated on a 1-5 scale) and to detect the presence of specific racial stereotypes (e.g., 'Angry Black person', 'Thug', 'Fatherless family').

Using an LLM-as-a-judge to detect geographic, cultural, and class-based stereotypes (e.g., 'backwards/rural', 'uneducated', 'poor/working class') in model responses triggered by Southern dialect prompts.
